naturalFeature.note: State GIS #139 and #140 are different waterfalls. Upper field point differs from GIS; avoid routing by ambiguous map pins.

publicLand.note: Visit Keweenaw identifies the lower falls as state land; regional reporting credits DNR and The Nature Conservancy with a published alternate public approach. This does not establish every intervening parcel or current gate.

seasonalArrival.note: 2026–27 Keweenaw visitor guide directs via Mandan Road to Fish Cove, while the 2023 visitor article identifies a rustic parking area. A 2024 DNR/TNC-reported alternative uses Hoar Lake Loop then leaves the vehicle before a berm. These are distinct descriptions, not verified interchangeable parking coordinates.

walkingCorridor.note: Visit Keweenaw describes about one mile on an unmarked rocky shoreline track from Fish Cove to Lower Montreal. Regional 2024 coverage describes a 1.3 mile unnamed-road walk on a separate approach. Neither is a current signed/maintained route or a measured route to Upper Montreal.

currentConditions.note: No November 2026 official public road/parking/gate and uninterrupted foot corridor status established; do not claim winter driving, current opening, GPS parking or safe shoreline passage.

newConstruction.note: New finding: Copper Harbor Trails Club homepage says the Montreal Corridor is complete and announces a June 26 2027 celebration. However, CHTC's detailed KPT project story describes access to both falls in future tense, Michigan DNR's project page still describes 2026 construction, its July 2026 map marks RTPD approval rather than as-built walking connections, and CHTC's trail-status page does not give a dated Montreal-falls trailhead/parking opening. KORC's separate west-bank parking/connector remains permit-pending in its own 2026 notice. A complete long-distance corridor is not proof of a visitor-ready route or exact parking to either fall.

builderProjectPage.claim: 2026 Montreal Corridor will create purpose-built access to Upper and Lower Montreal Falls (future-tense text)

dnrProjectPage.claim: 2026 Montreal Corridor construction underway and continuing through season

dnrMap.claim: July 22 2026 official map identifies RTPD-approved east-side Montreal River segment, not a verified as-built trail-to-falls line

trailStatus.claim: Trail-status page mixes an Oct 23 season note with last-dated May 18 2026 listing; no Montreal Falls named route status, legal parking or precise waterfall spur

completionReconciliation.conclusion: Do not infer current November 2026 public parking, road gate permissions, Upper viewpoint GPS, continuous official Lower or Upper waterfall walking line, or open-now winter trail from a general corridor completion headline.
